properties.name: 3i Group
properties.description: One of the few private equity firms whose shares are traded publicly as a PLC. 3i is London based and is a member of the FTSE 100. Its investment focuses include energy and infrastructure.

properties.name: Amundi (Credit Agricole)
properties.description: Europe’s biggest asset manager, part of the group of the French Credit Agricole bank. Has around $1.8 trillion assets under management.

properties.name: Andurand Capital
properties.description: London-based oil and energy trading hedge fund run by Pierre Andurand.

properties.name: Appian Capital
properties.description: London-based private equity fund which invests solely in metals and mining.

properties.name: Arkesden Partners
properties.description: Investment advisory and private equity firm working on oil, mining and other energy deals.

properties.name: Autonomy Capital
properties.description: US-based hedge fund that is reportedly a big gambler on European carbon emissions. It is also known as a vulture fund speculating on debts of “emerging countries”. Involved in court case to chase debts from crisis-hit Puerto Rico.

properties.name: Aviva
properties.description: UK investment manager with over $600 billion assets under management.

properties.name: Axa
properties.address: AXA UK PLC: 20 Gracechurch Street, London, EC3V 0BG
properties.description: French insurance giant and fund manager. Manages over $1 trillion.

properties.name: Bain Capital
properties.description: Founded by former US vice-president Mitt Romney (with other partners), known for its political links and for buying out and asset-stripping companies.

properties.name: Bank of New York Mellon Corporation
properties.description: US bank and fund manager overseeing around $2 trillion.

properties.name: BB Energy
properties.address: BB House, 12-14 Ansdell Street, London, W8 5BN
properties.description: Describes itself as “one of the world's leading independent energy trading companies” and “one of the most active gas, oil, gasoline, bitumen and fuel oil traders in the Mediterranean.”

properties.name: BlackRock Inc
properties.address: 12 Throgmorton Avenue, Drapers Gardens, London, EC2N 2DL
properties.description: The world’s biggest investment manager, managing over $7 trillion worth of assets (another report in the Financial Times says as much as $9 trillion). Basically, it owns shares in pretty much every major listed company in the world. This makes BlackRock a massively powerful institution that influences every aspect of global capitalism. Based in the US, it is “the world’s biggest backer of fossil fuel companies”, according to the Black Rock’s Big Problem campaign.

properties.name: Blackstone Group
properties.description: The world’s biggest private equity fund, according to PEI international. Headquartered in New York, it owns numerous well and less known companies and hotel chains. (NB: don’t confuse with BlackRock.) CEO Schwarzman was a major backer and adviser of President Trump. Its real estate division is infamous for its role in evictions and gentrification of cities, and has been targeted by resistance from Athens to Barcelona. Its Brazilian firms have been identified as “significantly responsible for the ongoing destruction of the Amazon rainforest”.

properties.name: Brevan Howard
properties.description: One of Europe’s biggest hedge funds. It makes short-term bets on commodities such as oil and metals prices, as well as currencies and more. Officially registered in Jersey and Cayman Islands tax havens. Sponsors financial analysis centre at Imperial College London.

properties.name: Capital Group
properties.description: US fund manager overseeing at least $1.7 trillion.

properties.name: Carlyle Group
properties.description: US-based. World’s fourth biggest PE fund, according to PEI international rankings. Perhaps best known for its links to the Bush and Bin Laden families. It is one of the owners of Neptune Energy, a fast-growing oil company active in the North Sea, Africa and South-East Asia.

properties.name: CVC Group
properties.description: The biggest UK-based PE fund, and the world’s third biggest, according to PEI international rankings. Its many investments across Europe, Asia and Americas include the UK’s biggest oil pipeline, and North Sea oil company Neptune.

properties.name: EIG Global Energy Partners
properties.address: 20 St. James’s Street, 7th Floor, London, SW1A 1ES
properties.description: Specialist fund investing in oil and gas, pipelines, and “alternative energy”. Has invested $37 billion in over 370 energy companies or projects over the years, including the Brazil-Bolivia gas pipeline (GASBOL), coal and oil sands in Canada, biomass in Spain, and numerous oil drillers from Alaska to Africa.

properties.name: Elliott Advisors
properties.description:
Infamous as a “vulture fund” which buys up and chases “distressed debt”. In particular, Elliott played a major role in suing the Argentinian and Peruvian governments for bond payments during the Latin American debt crisis. Other recent investments include buying football club AC Milan. 

Owned by Republican-backing US billionaire Paul Singer; the London office is run by his son, Gordon. It also owns bookshop chains Waterstones and Barnes and Noble. 

See also Corporate Watch’s investigation into Elliott and Waterstones.
properties.address notes: NB: official registered office address, but not confirmed as an operational base for the company.

properties.name: Fidelity
properties.description: Major US-based global investment manager, with over $3.3 trillion assets under management.

properties.name: GAM
properties.description: Swiss hedge fund mainly involved in gambling on bond markets, also has funds investing in energy companies.

properties.name: GNRI
properties.description: Private equity firm which invests in oil, gas and mining. Was a former unit of Barclays Bank bought out by its managers in 2015.

properties.name: Helios Investment Partners
properties.address: 2nd floor, 12 Charles II Street, London, SW1Y 4QU
properties.description: London-based private equity firm set up to deal in Africa, including investments in African oil companies.

properties.name: Insight Investment
properties.description: UK-based fund manager with around $900 billion assets under management.

properties.name: Kerogen Capital
properties.description: Private equity investor specialising in oil and gas companies, with bases in Hong Kong and London. Has been a major investor in North Sea oil companies, and in Energean, the UK-Greek-Israeli company drilling wells and building pipelines in the Eastern Mediterranean.

properties.name: KKR
properties.description: US private equity fund, the world’s second biggest according to PEI international rankings. Infamous for its “asset-stripping” company buyouts in the 1980s and 90s. Its investment focuses include oil and gas companies and related infrastructure, and real estate. In December 2019, KKR announced it was buying a 65% stake in the Canadian Coastal GasLink fracked gas pipeline, jointly with Canadian state investment fund AIMCo. The pipeline project is being vigorously resisted by Wetʼsuwetʼen first nations people. Wetʼsuwetʼen Solidarity activists occupied KKR’s London offices in 2020 to protest against the pipeline.

properties.name: Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA)
properties.address: Wren House, 15 Carter Lane, London, EC4V 5EY
properties.description: Controls $533 billion of assets. Its London division, called Kuwait Investment Office (KIO), makes investments across Europe and beyond. This, in turn, has a subsidiary infrastructure fund called Wren House (after its HQ). Wren House’s portfolio includes Britain’s biggest port operator ABP, London City Airport, and North Sea Midstream Partners, which controls a “major chunk of North Sea energy infrastructure” in Scotland.

properties.name: Lansdowne Partners
properties.description: “One of London’s oldest and most secretive hedge funds”, according to the Financial Times. It is perhaps best known for betting on the collapse of Northern Rock during the financial crash, and also has an energy fund speculating on oil and other commodity prices. It recently announced its plan to launch a spinoff company called ‘Clean Energy Transition’ in late 2021.

properties.name: Legal and General IM
properties.address: LGIM: One Coleman Street, London, EC2R 5AA
properties.description: UK insurance company and fund manager. The biggest UK-based investment manager, controlling over $1.2 trillion in assets.

properties.name: Man Group
properties.address: Riverbank House, 2 Swan Lane, London, EC4R 3AD
properties.description: The third-largest publicly traded hedge fund, and the biggest based in the UK. Its multiple funds gamble on pretty much anything from “natural catastrophe bonds” to real estate. It sponsors an Oxford University research centre and used to sponsor the Man Booker literature prize.

properties.name: Mandara Energy
properties.description: Specialist energy derivatives trader – i.e., makes bets for clients on oil and other energy prices. Based in London and Singapore.

properties.name: Monarch Alternative Capital
properties.description:
US-based vulture fund which specialises in buying and chasing “distressed debt”. Involved in court case to chase debts from crisis-hit Puerto Rico.  

Another string to its bow is investing in coal: “In February 2017, it became the principal shareholder in Arch Coal, the second largest supplier of coal to power companies in the U.S. Arch Coal has been accused by United Mine Workers of America of conspiring with Peabody Energy in a scheme to default on $1.3 billion in retiree pension and healthcare obligations.”

properties.name: Norges Bank IM / NGPFG
properties.address: Norges Bank IM: Queensberry House, 3 Old Burlington Street, London, W1S 3AE
properties.description: Norway’s massive oil reserve fund, administered by the state-owned Norges Bank Investment Management. The biggest SWF with just under $1.2 trillion in AUM. It acts much like the big investment funds above – similar to BlackRock or Vanguard, it owns shares in almost all the world’s big listed companies. Although, with Norway’s social democratic record, Norges Bank’s investments have long been a contentious issue, and campaigns over the years have succeeded in getting it to divest from many arms manufacturers, coal miners, gold miners, and others. It still invests in many of the companies on this map, however.

properties.name: Northern Trust Corporation, Inc
properties.address: 50 Bank Street, Canary Wharf, London, E14 5NT
properties.description: US fund manager overseeing over $1.2 trillion.

properties.name: Northlander Commodities
properties.address: Shearwater House, 21 The Green, Richmond, London TW9 1PX
properties.description: A “UK fund with strong ties to the US”, specialised in energy trading. Reported to have “made as much as $125 million” by speculating on global heating through trading carbon emission credits.

properties.name: Oaktree
properties.description: Major global private equity and investment fund, notorious as one of the biggest “distressed debt” or “vulture” funds – buying up the assets of crisis-hit countries and companies, then chasing them for repayment. It was a major profiteer from the European debt crisis, and recently involved in court cases to chase the debt of Puerto Rico. It also runs a $2.7 billion energy fund investing in oil tankers, pipeline infrastructure and more.

properties.name: Orion Resource Partners
properties.description:
Specialist metals and mining investment fund. Was previously part of Red Kite, spun off under its chief Oskar Lewinowski. Has invested in numerous mining companies including Dalradian. 

See also Corporate Watch’s investigation into Dalradian.

properties.name: OTC Europe
properties.description: Trading firm “specializing in over-the-counter energy physical and financial futures and options, including crude oil, gas oil, fuel, freight, and middle distillates”.

properties.name: Pimco (Allianz)
properties.description: Allianz is a giant German insurance and financial services company, which also now owns Pimco – a massive global investment fund specialising in bonds. Pimco alone controls $1.9 trillion assets under management, the bulk of the $2.5 trillion Allianz manages overall.

properties.name: Point 72
properties.description: Global hedge fund of US billionaire Steven Cohen. Point72 is the successor to Cohen’s previous business SAC Capital Advisors, which closed down after being hit by a $1.8 billion fine for insider trading.

properties.name: Prudential
properties.address: Grand Buildings, 1-3 Strand, Trafalgar Square, London, WC2N 5HR
properties.description: US fund manager – not to be confused with the UK’s Prudential PLC (which is also on this map). Manages $1.6 trillion.

properties.name: Prudential PLC
properties.description: UK insurer and fund manager, dating back to 1848 (NB: don’t confuse with the bigger Prudential from the US).

properties.name: Qatar Investment Authority (QIA)
properties.address: Qatari Diar: 16 Grosvenor Street, London, W1K 4QF
properties.description:
QIA is a major investor in many of the companies on our primary list. It is one of the biggest investors in mining giant Glencore, Russian oil and gas megacorp Rosneft, oil supermajor Total, French motorways and infrastructure giant Vinci, and many more. It also has large holdings in a number of global banks, notably Barclays. QIA has over $40 billion invested in the UK and plays a particularly important role for us as a major property owner in London. 

It owns 20% of Heathrow Airport, and a majority stake in the Canary Wharf Development Company – London’s biggest landlord, which owns the effectively privatised financial district. It also owns an 8% stake in the London Stock Exchange and is bidding to up that share to 31%. Plus it holds major stakes in Sainsburys and International Airlines Group, which owns BA and many other airlines. Some of its property is held through a subsidiary called Qatari Diar, a real estate investment fund which has bought further swathes of London from the Shard to the former Olympic Village.

properties.name: Red Kite Capital
properties.address: 2 Queen Anne's Gate Buildings, Dartmouth Street, London, England, SW1H 9BP
properties.description: Specialised metal and mining investment fund run by former Conservative party treasurer, and evangelical Christian, Lord Michael Farmer – called “Mr Copper” for his exalted position in the copper trading business. Its RK Mine Finance fund has lent money to numerous metals and mining companies. Also in the business is Farmer’s son, George, who has headed the UK branch of US right wing propaganda organisation Turning Point.
properties.address notes: NB: Registered address. This is a current official company address; but it is not confirmed that it is an operational site rather than just a “letterbox”.

properties.name: Riverstone
properties.description: Private equity firm focused on energy companies, with over $40 billion of investments in companies worldwide. Investments have included coal, oil drilling, biofuels, and much more. Invests in UK fracking firm Cuadrilla.

properties.name: Sculptor Capital
properties.description: Formerly called Och-Ziff, Sculptor is a global hedge fund founded by US billionaire Daniel Och. It is notorious for a 2016 corruption scandal where Och and his fund were accused by the US courts of paying over $100 million in bribes to secure natural resources deals in Libya, Nigeria, Guinea and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Among the companies it backed was New Age (African Global Energy), also on this map.

properties.name: Standard Life Aberdeen
properties.address: Bow Bells House, 1 Bread Street, London, EC4M 9HH
properties.description: UK fund manager, has over $600 billion assets under management.

properties.name: State Street Corporation
properties.address: 20 Churchill Pl, Canary Wharf, London, E14 5HJ
properties.description: US bank and one of the world’s biggest investment managers, with over $3 trillion assets managed.

properties.name: Temasek Holdings
properties.description: Singaporean SWF with $417 billion to spend. It has its European base in London. Temasek’s portfolio includes worldwide investments in oil and other energy companies, agribusiness and life sciences, industrials and transport, real estate, and more. It holds a majority share in Olam, the multinational agribusiness and palm oil producer accused of significant deforestation (see: Agribusiness).

properties.name: Vanguard Group
properties.description: The second-biggest global investor, coming close to BlackRock with over $6 trillion managed – or over $7 trillion, according to the Financial Times. Largely an “index” investor that allocates funds to every major company on the world’s exchanges – including, of course, many of the biggest polluters.

properties.name: Warburg Pincus
properties.address: Almack House, 28 King Street, London, SW1Y 6QW
properties.description: US based. One of the top ten global PE funds, according to PEI international rankings.

properties.name: Winton Capital
properties.address: Grove House, 27 Hammersmith Grove, London, W6 0NE
properties.description: One of the biggest London-based hedge funds, a “quant fund” which uses maths-heavy data analysis and computer algorithms to speculate on commodities across the world. The associated David and Claudia Harding Foundation has given £100 million to Cambridge University.
